svg.title: 16-bit Pipelined Datapath, ISA v1.4 — connected logical overview
svg.desc: Native editable vector diagram rebuilt from the user's two reference images and current RTL. Main data, STR data, forwarding, tags and control have fixed typed endpoints. External RAM registered outputs supply logical IF/ID and MEM/WB data boundaries.

g.title: E01: PC_fetch / im_addr → im.addr. Full address is exported; only low index bits reach native RAM.
E03: PC_fetch captured as d_pc → ifid.pc. PC tag is captured for an accepted fetch slot. An out-of-range slot carries fetch_fault while physical IM is disabled.
E04: im_en → im.en. im_en = fetch_accept AND fetch_in_range.
E05: im_dout → decode.inst. Registered IM dout directly drives d_inst / decoder. No IR.
E06: d_rd / d_rs → rf.raddr. Each register index is 2 bits, never [2:0].
E07: d_imm[7:0] / sign_mode → ext.imm. Decoder, not RF, supplies immediate and extension mode.
E08: control intents / use masks / illegal → idex.decodeControl.
E09: d_pc / d_valid / d_fetch_fault → idex.Dtags. Decode illegal joins d_fetch_fault before X capture.
E13: x_imm_ext → muxB.imm. Immediate bypasses operand_forward.
E23: rd_fwd → exmem.storeIn. Only rd_fwd takes this orange path. It never enters MUX/ALU or WB.
E25: x_pc16 / imm8 / relative intent → target.args. Captured instruction PC and imm8 feed branch_target16, not ALU result.
E26: X PC / destination / intents / valid / fault → exmem.tagsIn. Per-instruction PC/destination/intents/valid/fault bypass the ALU.
E27: m_exec_value → memGuard.EA. EA is checked, but its exported value is unchanged.
E28: m_exec_value → memwb.execIn. Ordinary value passes separately from DM load output.
E29: m_exec_value → dm.addr. Full EA checked before physical index truncation.
E30: m_exec_value → forward.M. Ready non-load M value with valid/fault/RW/destination qualification. M access fault makes it ineligible.
E32: dm_din = m_store_data → dm.din. dm_din is a separate always-exported value; dm_we determines the actual write.
E35: dm_dout = w_load_data → wbmux.load. Registered DM dout directly drives the WB load input. No MDR.
E37: m_access_fault → memwb.memoryFault. M access fault creates a valid W fault token.
E42: w_valid / w_fault / w_halt / w_pc → stop.tags. Tags reach stop handling independently of write enables and flags_reg.
E43: wb_data → forward.W. Selected WB result, never a raw load address.
E44: wb_data → rf.wdata. RF write data and explicit same-address WB-to-ID bypass.
E45: w_rd[1:0] / rf_we → rf.wcontrol. Qualified w_rd/rf_we accompany the selected WB data.
E46: m_cmp_z + M CMP qualification → zselect.M. Only eligible M CMP candidates can bypass saved Z.
E47: w_cmp_z + W CMP qualification → zselect.W. Eligible W CMP candidate, lower priority than M CMP.
E48: saved architectural Z → zselect.saved. Only architectural Z feeds branch selection; C/V are not branch predicates in this ISA.
E49: branch_target → coord.rawTarget. Raw target enters arbitration; only a qualified redirect reaches PC.
E50: z_effective → coord.Zpredicate. z_effective participates in JZ request qualification, not EX/MEM ordinary data.
E51: X load/destination, validity and stop/branch intents → coord.Xevents. Load-use uses actual D sources and X load destination; EX legality/stop/branch logic is grouped.
E53: w_stop_token + pipeline drain → coord.Wstop. Final HALTED/FAULTED requires consumed W stop token and empty next pipeline.
E54: clk / rst → coord.clockReset. Clock/reset are broadcast to sequential core modules; RAM is not reset by rst.
E57: IF/ID hold / kill / valid → ifid.occupancy.
E61: STR bubble / valid fault token → memwb.occupancy.
E64: control intents / use masks / illegal → coord.DactualSources. D masks/indices combine with the aligned D valid/fault tags; unused fields never create false load-use dependencies.
DM 256 × 16 — Vivado/rtl/sync_memories.v
g.text: en=0 holds dout; no RAM reset

g.title: operand_forward — Vivado/rtl/operand_forward.v
g.text: Rd/Rs independently: ready M > W > captured operand
Newest unready M load blocks older same-register

g.title: alu16 + CLA16 — Vivado/rtl/alu16.v
g.text: result16; eq / C / V are candidates
Flag writes occur only under WB masks

g.title: Z selection — Vivado/rtl/datapath_core.sv
g.text: M CMP > W CMP > saved Z

g.title: MEM access guard — Vivado/rtl/datapath_core.sv
g.text: MR / MW are read / write intents

g.title: STR data path — Vivado/rtl/datapath_core.sv
g.text: Qualified write at MEM ending edge

g.title: Pipeline coordination (hardwired logic inside core) — Vivado/rtl/datapath_core.sv
g.text: Inputs: D actual sources, X load / stop / branch intents, M access fault, W stop token
Load-use: hold PC + IF/ID, inject EX bubble; older MEM/WB stages still advance
Reset > older MEM fault > EX fault/HALT > qualified redirect > load-use
RUN / DRAIN_HALT / DRAIN_FAULT → HALTED / FAULTED only after stop-token drain
ISA v1.4 / Single issue, in order / 16-bit word addresses
datapath_core · 87 logical I/O bits · memories are external
* IF/ID and MEM/WB are logical RAM-data boundaries. Registered IM/DM outputs already exist; the core adds no IR/MDR.
Dots mark true fanouts. Crossings without dots are unconnected. Gray paths carry grouped instruction tags, indices and intents.
Logical connection diagram from ISA v1.4 RTL, not a Vivado RTL Analysis capture. Static source review; no new simulation claim.
